title: The Scientific Revolution
key_facts: Emphasis on observation, mathematics, and experimentation transformed natural philosophy
Landmark works include Copernicus’s De revolutionibus (1543) and Newton’s Principia (1687)
New institutions and networks (academies, correspondence) spread findings
causes: Renaissance humanism and recovery of classical texts
Printing press enabling rapid dissemination of ideas
Patronage and competition among states and scholars
outcome: Heliocentric astronomy, new mechanics, and experimental method
Standardization of measurement and mathematical modeling
Foundation for modern science and technology
impacts: Accelerated technological progress and scientific institutions
Shaped Enlightenment thought and secular inquiry
